verses.1: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
verses.3: Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night in which it was said, A man is conceived.
verses.4: Let that day be darkness; may God not seek it from above, nor let a ray of light shine upon it.
verses.5: Let darkness take it, and a shadow of death dwell over it. Let a gloom cover it like the morning of the sun.
verses.6: Let the night perish which brought me forth, may it not be counted among the days of the year, nor registered in the months.
verses.7: Let that night be desolate; may no sound of joy enter it.
verses.8: May those who curse the day be cursed, the one who is ready to rouse the leviathan.
verses.9: Let the stars of that night be darkened; may it wait for light but find none, nor see the dawning of day.
verses.10: For it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb, and would have hidden the pain from my eyes.
verses.11: Why did I not die at birth, why emerge from the womb and see trouble?
verses.12: Why did my knees receive me, and why did my breasts nurse me?
verses.13: For now I would have lain down and been at rest; I would have slept and been free from my distress.
verses.14: With kings and counselors of the land, who built their cities in ruins.
verses.15: Or with princes who had gold, whose houses were filled with silver.
verses.16: Or like a miscarriage hidden from the womb, like infants who have not seen light.
verses.17: There the wicked cease from their turmoil, and there the weary of strength find rest.
verses.18: The prisoners there are at peace, for they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
verses.19: Small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
verses.20: Why give light to one who toils, and life to one who is embittered in soul?
verses.21: Those who wait for death and it comes not, who dig for it like hidden treasures.
verses.22: The happy ones are those who find their grave, for they are at peace.
verses.23: For a man whose way is hidden, and God has walled him in.
verses.24: For before my bread I have sorrow, and my groans pour out like water.
verses.25: For I feared what I dreaded, and it has come to me; what I dreaded I have found.
verses.26: I did not find peace, nor rest, nor quiet, but trouble has come to me.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The Hebrew uses "cursed" (קָלַל) in the context of lament, not a full-blown imprecation, as per the tone of the chapter.
- v. 4: “a ray of light” translates פְּנֵי נְהָרָה, a rare phrase, here rendered as a ray or beam of light.
- v. 10: “would have hidden the pain” is an implied counterfactual based on the conditional structure used in the verse.
- v. 25: The phrase “what I dreaded I have found” reflects the poetic parallelism of the Hebrew.
